beare_usage: memory — a state (ἕξις) or affection (πάθος) of perception or conception, conditioned by the lapse of time, directed exclusively at the past; belongs essentially to the primary faculty of sense-perception.
notes: Technical sense: the dispositional state directed at the past. Distinguished from recollection (ἀνάμνησις).

beare_usage: recollection — a distinct quasi-inferential process (ζήτησις) of recovering memory through deliberate sequential reactivation of movements; belongs only to beings with the deliberative faculty.
notes: Beare: 'recollecting'; differs fundamentally from Platonic ἀνάμνησις (recovery of innate knowledge). Sorabji prefers 'recollection.' Aristotle's ἀνάμνησις is a psychological-physiological process, not metaphysical recovery of Forms.

beare_usage: image — the sensory image serving as the medium of memory; functions dually as an object of contemplation in itself (θεώρημα) and as a likeness (εἰκών) of the thing remembered.
notes: The dual-aspect structure of the φάντασμα is central to the treatise's argument. The painted-panel analogy (450b20-451a2) is the key explanatory passage.

beare_usage: imagination — the image-producing faculty treated in De Anima III.3; all objects of imagination are potentially objects of memory; without imagination, thinking is impossible.
notes: Presupposed from De Anima III.3. The φαντασία-φάντασμα relation is foundational for the memory account.

beare_usage: movement — the residual physiological movement left by perception; chains of such movements constitute the mechanism of both memory and recollection.
notes: In De Memoria, κίνησις refers specifically to residual perceptual movements, not locomotion as in MA or Physics.

beare_usage: the primary perceptive faculty / common sense — the faculty by which one cognizes magnitude, motion, and time; the organ to which memory essentially belongs.
notes: Identical with κοινὴ αἴσθησις. Bridges De Memoria to De Sensu and De Anima III.1-2.

beare_usage: time — the necessary condition of memory: all memory implies the lapse of time; recollection involves perception of time as magnitude.
notes: Presupposes Physics IV.10-14 on time as the number of motion.

beare_usage: impression — the quasi-physical mark stamped in the soul and its bodily seat by perception; analogous to a seal-ring impression in wax.
notes: The wax-seal analogy echoes Plato's Theaetetus 191c-e, but Aristotle integrates it within his hylomorphic psychology.

beare_usage: state/affection — memory is defined as a ἕξις or πάθος of perception/conception conditioned by time; ἕξις = settled dispositional state; πάθος = modification undergone by soul and body.
notes: Both terms are ontological categories with extensive use across the Aristotelian corpus.

beare_usage: likeness — the relational aspect of the φάντασμα: when the soul perceives the image qua related to something else, it functions as a likeness and enables memory.
notes: The εἰκών/θεώρημα distinction is the core of the dual-aspect analysis of the memory-image.

beare_usage: deliberative faculty — recollection belongs naturally to those who possess it, since recollection is itself a kind of investigation (ζήτησις) and deliberation is a form of inference.
notes: Links recollection to deliberation and thus to the practical domain.

beare_usage: starting-point — the initial term from which the recollective search proceeds; the middle of a series is the optimal starting-point for search in both directions.
notes: The recollective starting-points (τόποι) are structurally parallel to rhetorical topoi.
